source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 256 (2026), article 106266; publisher theorem text inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published article studies nonparametric distance-based BDD estimation/inference and minimax lower bounds for isotropic regression estimators; the primary endpoint did not expose theorem text for a formula-level comparison.
Dong estimates scalar rounded-running-variable RD under polynomial regression specifications and known within-rounding-cell moments, with explicit correction formulas.

The article studies RD with a moderately discrete scalar running variable, rejects clustered-by-score intervals as protection against misspecification, and proposes two coverage-guaranteed alternatives under conditional-mean restrictions.
The article derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for linear functionals over convex regression classes, including an RD specialization.
The article constructs bias-aware honest intervals for scalar nonparametric targets using kernel or local-polynomial estimators under smoothness restrictions.

Under correct treatment classification and smooth potential-outcome conditional means in the observed running variable, the paper gives a causal interpretation for the effect at the observed cutoff and discusses discreteness or irregular support.

The paper establishes that continuous running-variable measurement error destroys ordinary RD identification and recovers LATE identification using auxiliary discrepancy data under nondifferential-error and completeness conditions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Davezies and Le Barbanchon (2017) and Gerard, Rokkanen, and Rothe (2020), then state a precise non-subsumption comparison: no auxiliary true-score sample, deterministic annular coarsening, a fixed bivariate point target, and an order-Δ fiber result.

Promote the sharp release-fiber endpoint program from OEQ to the main advance by solving it on a nontrivial released-law subclass and proving that its endpoints are strictly tighter than the universal 4LΔ envelope.
Strengthen the statistical contribution with the sharp transition experiment for Δ n^(1/4)→κ, including a κ-indexed leading constant or an optimal honest interval rather than only rate orders.
Remove ass:radial-bernoulli as a separate assumption; retain bounded outcomes as a class property and state explicitly that Bernoulli laws are used only for the lower-bound witnesses.
